results.summary: This project implements a finite state machine (FSM) combined with a counter to simulate a traffic light controller for two perpendicular streets. It was developed as part of the Digital Systems course at Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile. The design supports normal mode with priority for Street A and a parade mode where Street B stays green indefinitely. It requires external LEDs and push-buttons for testing and can be simulated using cocotb.

This design implements a serial data pipeline that combines SERDES, a 4-tap FIR filter, and XOR encryption. It deserializes 8-bit words from a serial input, filters and encrypts them, then serializes the result. The design includes a done pulse to indicate completion of each byte transmission. It requires no external hardware and can be tested with a logic analyzer or LEDs.

This project is a fully synthesizable, stream-oriented SHA-256 implementation that processes a byte stream and outputs a 256-bit digest. It consists of a compression core, a ROM for constants, a byte-stream front-end, and a GPIO wrapper with a skid buffer. The design uses a simple handshake interface and requires no special peripherals. It is notable for its efficient implementation and Tiny Tapeout compatibility.

This project implements a modified version of the Simon Says game using digital logic and memory elements to store a pseudo-random sequence of colors. It interfaces with external buttons and LEDs for gameplay. A Raspberry Pi is used to send an 8-bit seed and read a 2-bit state debug signal. The design requires six push buttons and four LEDs.

This is a simple VGA demo that displays a bitmap and allows color inversion via an input pin. It outputs standard VGA signals including RGB and sync. The design was tested on VGA playground and requires a VGA PMOD for external connection. The documentation is minimal but sufficient to understand its function.

This project displays an animated dance of navy-blue and yellow figures synchronized with the San Jose State Fight Song for the first 15 seconds. It outputs VGA signals and audio through a sound PMOD. The design requires a VGA monitor and speaker connected via appropriate PMODs. The documentation is brief but indicates the intended behavior.

This project is an 8-bit basic ALU unit with 8-bit instructions. It uses separate instruction address and data buses, with a write enable signal. The documentation is extremely thin, providing no details on operation or testing beyond vague statements. It appears to be a simple educational design but lacks sufficient information for thorough understanding.

This design generates a bouncing ball pattern with an SJSU-themed backdrop on a VGA display. It automatically starts upon power-up and requires a Tiny Tapeout VGA PMOD. The documentation is minimal, stating that details will be explained later, but the basic functionality is clear from the description and pins.

This project implements a spiking neural network with STDP and reward-based learning. It consists of 8 layers, each with 2 neurons, and weights are loaded from memory. The design accepts 32 4-bit weights and 2 input values to execute. The documentation is brief but provides enough to understand the basic operation and testing procedure.

This project implements an adaptive leaky integrate-and-fire spiking neuron core for edge AI. It features a 12-bit membrane potential with configurable decay, adaptive threshold, and a 3-cycle refractory period. The design outputs the membrane potential, spike, and spike count. It is intended for low-power neural network applications and includes learning mode control.
